newsitem.title: USA: Cross-Cont sees Q2 results below expectations.
newsitem.headline: Cross-Cont sees Q2 results below expectations.

text.p: Cross-Continent Auto Retailers Inc said Wednesday its earnings per share for the second quarter ending June 30 will be $0.07 below analysts' expectations of $0.25 cents.
The company attributed the worse-than-expected earnings to about $717,000 in operating losses, or $0.05 per share, at its Performance Nissan and Performance Dodge dealerships in April and May.
It also cited lower-than-expected new vehicle sales at Lynn Hickey Dodge because the Chrysler engine plant strike disrupted the flow of new cars.

"Morgan Stanley had us at 24 cents (per share earnings) on the (second) quarter. Take five cents off for the operating losses, take off another 2 cents for the Chrysler strike, and that puts us at about 17 cents for the quarter," said John Gaines, the company's vice president of finance.
A First Call consensus estimate in April put the company's second-quarter earnings at $0.25 per share.
The company said in a statement it expected its full-year results will be "negatively impacted by these events." Gaines declined to predict the full-year earnings.

The company also said it agreed to sell its Performance Nissan and Performance Dodge dealerships for about $9 million to Emmett Rice, Cross Continent's chief operating officer. Rice will pay in Cross-Auto shares for the dealerships and will quit the company as part of the deal, the company said.
The Performance Nissan dealership posted about $32 million in revenues last year and the Performance Dodge dealership reported $46 million, the company said.
The company's stock closed unchanged at 12 today.
